topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Data Efficiency
explanation: The Memory Hierarchy is a tiered storage structure organized by proximity to the CPU, trading capacity and cost for reduced access latency. This structure ranges from fast, small SRAM caches (L1, L2, L3) to slower, larger DRAM main memory. Caching strategies exploit temporal and spatial locality by migrating frequently accessed data blocks into these higher-speed levels. The primary goal is to maximize the cache hit rate, significantly minimizing the Average Memory Access Time (AMAT). Effective cache management utilizes specific mapping functions (e.g., set-associative) and replacement policies (e.g., LRU) to maintain data coherence and optimize the utilization of limited cache capacity.
